test_title: SSC Selection Post Graduation Level Official Paper (Held on: 3 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Speak of the devil

options.text: The person we were just talking about showed up
The person we were talking about was guilty
The person we were talking about never appeared
The person we were talking about was a devil in disguise

solution:
The correct answer is: **The person we were just talking about showed up**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The idiom "**Speak of the devil**" means something you say when the person you were talking about appears unexpectedly. 

 
 
• For example- *Did you hear what happened to Anna yesterday - oh, speak of the devil, here she is.*
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the idiom "**Speak of the devil**" is "**The person we were just talking about showed up**."
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.
